holds.evidence: Small-type Zenobius 6.47 note attributes a statement to Herodotus; Bergk assigned it to Herodas because it does not appear in Herodotus. It is not a printed authorial body fragment and was already retained as an editorial source note by the role review.
holds.label: IXc source note

holds.evidence: Commentary introduces a corrupt proverb as possibly choliambic (Xa, Crusius 70), then calls the following proposal Xb a still longer venture. The discussion continues on PDF page 483.
holds.label: Xa; Xb beginning

holds.evidence: Commentary says Herodas is only one of many choliambic writers, identifies Crusius 66 with Phoenix and 65 with Callimachus, and discusses other uncertain fragments. Its Greek quotations are not wholesale Herodas authorial text.
holds.label: Xb; other doubtful quotations

holds.evidence: The two Greek lines at PDF y=238.1–260.2 are anonymous courtesan speech quoted from Strabo 371. The commentary on printed page 417 says the subject may have been such a discussion and I would refer the fragment XIa here: this is conjectural attribution.
holds.label: XIa

holds.evidence: Commentary describes the quotation from Herodian through Etymologicum Magnum page 19 as anonymous, saying here too may belong (XIb, Crusius 69). No secure Herodas attribution is supplied.
holds.label: XIb

holds.evidence: Printed page 419/PDF 489 explicitly identifies these Greek lines as renderings by Headlam with additional renderings by Knox of Latin Mattius. It says their status as translations is uncertain and their dependence on Herodas doubly uncertain. Greek language and body-sized type do not make these ancient Herodas.
holds.label: XII: modern Greek renderings of Mattius

holds.evidence: The edition calls the papyrus unplaced and prints only ξυ with faint remains of letters below. It supplies neither a word nor a verse location. Its note maps the older XIV and XV numbers to IXa and IXb, which are already represented on PDF page 472.
holds.label: unplaced papyrus (under XIII, XIV, XV)

qualification: This inventory covers the Greek authorial body printed in the pinned 1922 edition: Mimes I–VIII, IX with IXa/IXb, X, and XI. It is not a claim that the ancient works survive complete. The 62 existing primary rows on 13 pages already represent those pages' complete printed authorial blocks; their identities and literal readings are preserved. Recovery concerns 22 source-disjoint missing body pages. Existing OCR spelling defects, critical restorations, dialogue distributions, and attribution variants are not silently resolved. VIII's printed lacunae and incomplete words remain lacunae and incomplete words. Anchors identify printed boundaries and are not replacement transcriptions or requirements that an OCR witness agree in spelling. Modern Greek renderings of Latin Mattius, anonymous or conjecturally attributed quotations, and the unplaced two-letter papyrus remain separately identified below. Facing English and scholarly notes are outside the authorial body.
